verdict.rationale: Jev exposes a versioned API surface: endpoints under /v1 such as POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. It also documents versioned model IDs with alias semantics (jev-latest, jev-preview) and tells users to pin a version and migrate on their own schedule. However, no deprecation policy is documented: there are no sunset timelines, notice periods, or retirement rules for old API or model versions. missing for 10: a documented deprecation/sunset policy with notice periods, API-version lifecycle docs beyond the /v1 path, independent corroboration of version stability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: If you have tuned confidence thresholds against a specific version, pin that version's ID instead of the alias and move to the new one on your own schedule.
Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`.
`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, with a description and release date for each
